elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the report as an 'integrative review', not explicitly as a 'systematic review' as required by the element description.

elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the aim/objective of the review.

elements.quote: Included studies were not restricted by research design; and had to evaluate the sustainability of an EBI in a healthcare context.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies inclusion criteria regarding research design and context.

elements.quote: a comprehensive search strategy was applied across five databases.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions five databases but does not name them or provide the dates they were last searched.

elements.quote: We assessed the methodological quality of studies using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the tool used to assess methodological quality/risk of bias.

elements.quote: Following Whittemore and Knafl's methodological process: (1) problem identification; (2) literature search; (3) data evaluation; (4) data analysis; and (5) presentation...
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methodological process used for analysis and presentation.

elements.quote: Of 18,783 articles retrieved, 64 fit the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (64) but does not report the number of participants.

elements.quote: Most studies (77%) did not measure sustainability outcomes, rather these studies focused on sustainability determinants.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results regarding sustainability outcomes and determinants.
The study is an integrative review and does not report conducting a meta-analysis.
The review synthesizes approaches and does not compare groups with direction of effect.

elements.quote: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used.
elements.reason: The abstract discusses findings and gaps but does not explicitly summarize limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency).

elements.quote: Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation and implications of the results.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: There is limited evidence to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) for healthcare improvement.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the current state of knowledge (limited evidence) and uncertainties regarding evaluating sustainability of EBIs.

elements.quote: Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The abstract explains the importance and need for the review by stating it offers recommendations and highlights importance to advance the field.

elements.quote: A focus on evaluation is what differentiates this review from recent syntheses published on approaches to sustainability research.
elements.reason: The discussion section acknowledges existing reviews (recent syntheses) and explains the specific need for this review (focus on evaluation vs determinants).
This is an integrative review of evaluation approaches, not a review of intervention effects, so the requirement to describe the mechanism of action of an intervention does not apply.

The provided text mentions frameworks, models, and theories used by included studies, but does not explicitly state that a logic model was considered in the review's rationale to show relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare.
elements.reason: The review objectives are explicitly stated in the Aim section, clearly defining the goal to identify and synthesize approaches.

elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.
elements.reason: The review focuses on identifying evaluation approaches rather than assessing intervention effects, so PICO comparisons are not applicable.

elements.quote: Articles were included if they: • Were published in a peer-review journal • Were primary research • Had explicit research design and data collection methods • Had an explicit theoretical approach... • Were within a healthcare setting • Evaluated the sustainability of an EBI
elements.reason: Specifies study design, setting, and research type, but does not explicitly specify follow-up requirements in the eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: We only included published studies in the English language and peer-reviewed primary studies in this review.
elements.reason: Explicitly specifies language (English) and publication status (peer-reviewed) as eligibility criteria.
The eligibility criteria do not distinguish between exclusion due to outcomes not being measured versus outcomes not being reported.

elements.quote: The two reviewers independently extracted the following variables: (1) study design, (2) evaluation type (independent versus composite)...
elements.reason: Extraction variables are listed which imply grouping, but explicit specification of synthesis groups linked to review objectives is not detailed in the methods text.
Restrictions on eligibility (e.g., English language, peer-reviewed) are stated, but rationales for these restrictions are not provided in the methods or eligibility section.

elements.quote: In December 2018 and July 2020, we searched the following databases
elements.reason: The text explicitly reports the dates (December 2018 and July 2020) when the databases were searched.

elements.quote: Ovid MEDLINE(R) and Epub Ahead of Print, In-Process and Other Non-Indexed Citations and Daily (1946 to current); OVID Embase (1974 to current); EBSCOhost CINAHL Plus with Full-text (1937 to current); Wiley Cochrane Library (inception to current)
elements.reason: The text reports the names of the databases (MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane), the search interfaces/platforms (Ovid, EBSCOhost, Wiley), and the available coverage dates for each.
The search strategy described was limited to bibliographic databases; no study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories were mentioned as being searched.
No websites, search engines, or other online sources were reported as being searched in the Methods section.
The text does not mention contacting any organisations or manufacturers to identify studies.
The text does not describe contacting any individuals to identify studies.
The search strategy focused on database searches; there is no report of examining reference lists of included studies.
No backward or forward citation searching is reported in the provided text.
The text does not report consulting specific journals or conference proceedings directly (e.g., hand-searching).

elements.quote: Additional file 1. Search strategy. The four databases searched on Dec 21, 2018, as well as an additional search in July 2020. The file depicts the date of searchers and strategy used, including all search terms in each database.
elements.reason: The supplementary information section explicitly states that Additional File 1 contains the full search strategy including all search terms for each database.

elements.quote: In December 2018 and July 2020, we searched the following databases: Ovid MEDLINE(R)... (1946 to current); OVID Embase (1974 to current); EBSCOhost CINAHL Plus with Full-text (1937 to current); Wiley Cochrane Library (inception to current).

elements.quote: In the first screening stage, one reviewer (RF) independently screened the abstracts and titles of all the citations retrieved from the database searches. A second reviewer (AB) independently screened a randomly selected 10% of all titles and abstracts to verify selection for inclusion or exclusion. In the second stage, two reviewers (RF and AB) independently screened all full-text articles that had passed first-stage screening.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states the number of reviewers for the first screening stage (one primary, one secondary for verification) and the second stage (two reviewers).

elements.quote: one reviewer (RF) independently screened... A second reviewer (AB) independently screened... two reviewers (RF and AB) independently screened
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that reviewers worked independently at both the title/abstract screening stage and the full-text screening stage.

elements.quote: We discussed any differences in screening at team meetings

No evidence in the retrieved text describes crowdsourcing platforms.
No evidence in the retrieved text describes previously screened datasets used to eliminate records.

elements.quote: A The two reviewers independently extracted the following variables
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that the two reviewers worked independently during extraction.

No evidence in the retrieved text specifies software used to extract data from figures.

elements.quote: We used the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) [17] to assess the methodological quality of studies.
elements.reason: The risk-of-bias tool (MMAT) and its citation are explicitly specified.

elements.quote: The MMAT [17] appraises the quality by study design type, such as quantitative, qualitative, or mixed empirical methods. The criteria are specific to each type of study, with five domains apportioned to qualitative studies and quantitative studies subdivided into randomized controlled, non-randomized and descriptive studies.
elements.reason: The domains and components assessed by the tool are described in detail.

elements.quote: Each study is assigned an overall quality score, using asterisks representing the quality appraisal of each study. Scores vary from 20% (*) when one criterion is met to 100% (*****) when all criteria are met.
elements.reason: An overall risk-of-bias judgement (score) is made and the rules for deriving it are reported.

elements.quote: We used the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) [17] to assess the methodological quality of studies.
elements.reason: No adaptations to the existing tool were mentioned; the standard tool was used as is.

elements.quote: We used the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) [17] to assess the methodological quality of studies.
elements.reason: No newly developed risk-of-bias tool was used; an existing tool (MMAT) was used.

elements.quote: Two reviewers independently completed MMAT assessments and compared scoring.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers, their independence, and disagreement-resolution procedures (comparing scoring) are reported.

elements.quote: We used the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) [17] to assess the methodological quality of studies.
elements.reason: No process to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators was described.

elements.quote: We used the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) [17] to assess the methodological quality of studies.
elements.reason: No automation tools were described for risk-of-bias assessment.

elements.quote: Data analysis followed the methodological steps outlined by Whittemore and Knafl [12] which included data reduction, data display, data comparison, and drawing conclusions and verifications.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes a narrative synthesis approach (Whittemore and Knafl) without specifying statistical effect measures (e.g., risk ratio, mean difference) for the synthesis of results.

elements.quote: Integrative reviews take a more flexible approach to analysis compared to systematic reviews, combining both quantitative and qualitative data if there are similarities [12-14].
elements.reason: The study is an integrative review using narrative synthesis; therefore, thresholds for interpreting effect sizes are not applicable.

elements.quote: Integrative reviews take a more flexible approach to analysis compared to systematic reviews, combining both quantitative and qualitative data if there are similarities [12-14].
elements.reason: No quantitative synthesis was performed; thus, methods to re-express results using another effect measure are not applicable.

elements.quote: Integrative reviews take a more flexible approach to analysis compared to systematic reviews, combining both quantitative and qualitative data if there are similarities [12-14].
